name: Midas Capital
rootCause: Blocksec: It is due to an unexcepted external call before updating critical variables->reentrancy & miscalculation of the token prices. The key points to make profits are: 1) the calculation of a position's collateral depends on self.D and totalSupply; 2) self.D is updated after an unexcepted callback, so the four borrows in step 5 to use an outdated self.D. Vulnerable code snippet: https://bscscan.com/address/0x13a2eb858aa1ace895a2a89ac6afd48bd6b1f8d7#code#F6#L335 Image from blocksec Attack tx: https://polygonscan.com/tx/0x0053490215baf541362fc78be0de98e3147f40223238d5b12512b3e26c0a2c2f Analysis: https://twitter.com/peckshield/status/1614774855999844352 https://twitter.com/BlockSecTeam/status/1614864084956254209 https://www.kalos.xyz/blog/midas-capital-hack-analysis https://blog.solidityscan.com/midas-capital-hack-analysis-ae59ed052729 https://neptunemutual.com/blog/understanding-midas-capital-exploit/

descriptions.text: The Midas touch has backfired, leaving a $660K hole in one of its jFIAT pools. The read-only reentrancy vulnerability is a known weakness of a recently introduced collateral type. Let’s hope this rushed decision doesn’t prove to be Midas’ undoing this time…

Blocksec: It is due to an unexcepted external call before updating critical variables->reentrancy & miscalculation of the token prices. The key points to make profits are: 1) the calculation of a position's collateral depends on self.D and totalSupply; 2) self.D is updated after an unexcepted callback, so the four borrows in step 5 to use an outdated self.D. Vulnerable code snippet: https://bscscan.com/address/0x13a2eb858aa1ace895a2a89ac6afd48bd6b1f8d7#code#F6#L335 Image from blocksec Attack tx: https://polygonscan.com/tx/0x0053490215baf541362fc78be0de98e3147f40223238d5b12512b3e26c0a2c2f Analysis: https://twitter.com/peckshield/status/1614774855999844352 https://twitter.com/BlockSecTeam/status/1614864084956254209 https://www.kalos.xyz/blog/midas-capital-hack-analysis https://blog.solidityscan.com/midas-capital-hack-analysis-ae59ed052729 https://neptunemutual.com/blog/understanding-midas-capital-exploit/

Due to the read-only-reentrancy problem (read-only-reentrancy) when interacting with the Curve liquidity pool, the cross-chain money market solution Midas Capital was attacked and exploited in the Polygon liquidity pool of the stablecoin protocol Jarvis, and has lost $650,000.
